title: Letters of Abbot Corvin Ashgrove
author: Abbot Corvin Ashgrove
notes: Bible 7.2: priory scriptorium, fragments. The abbot's own voice on the Long Vespers (before and after), cut short by damage. The "friend below" notes are mw-e39.42 and are not here.

pages.text:
To a correspondent in the city.

Anselm thinks it is a threat. It is a sentence, and we have spent three hundred years shouting over it. What if it is trying to tell us something? I have spent the winter at the foot of the shaft with a candle and a slate. It repeats. It is not noise. [illegible]

Later.

Anselm will not speak to me. The brothers keep the bell as they keep the Rule, which is to say without asking what it is for. I do not blame them. I will take out the tongue for one night only. One night, to listen.

I have told no one but you. If I am wrong, the bell is a day's work to put right. If I am right, [missing]
